experiment.steer: S015 §14 coherence states; §21 simulated is not physical

device.reason: fabric-level, no GPU in this path

transport.reason: no external GPU exists; §21 forbids citing any transport number here as physical evidence

headline: A PARTIAL LOSS CANNOT REUSE THE FULL-LOSS HANDLER, AND A ROUND-TRIP CHECK DOES NOT VALIDATE THE RESIDENT COPY. The first is the last named-absent failure mode; the second is a blind spot the corruption receipt could not see because it was looking at the wrong path.
what_the_previous_receipt_named: still not modelled: a provider that corrupts CONSISTENTLY in both directions, corruption AFTER the check, and A PARTIAL DEVICE LOSS where some memory survives

partial_loss.why_it_cannot_reuse_the_full_handler: device_lost is safe because of a BLANKET ASSUMPTION -- nothing in that domain survived. On a partial loss that assumption is WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Assume everything survived and valid_copies() names PHANTOMS. Assume everything died and a DIRTY copy the device still holds becomes MANUFACTURED DATA LOSS -- the fabric destroying live state that was never gone.
partial_loss.so_the_fabric_asks: device_partially_lost PROBES each copy through the provider and classifies per object. A partial loss is the case where the bookkeeping CANNOT BE DERIVED and has to be MEASURED.
partial_loss.demonstrated: two objects in the domain, ONE allocation cleared: survived=['KEPT'], lost=['GONE'], and valid_copies() follows both ways
partial_loss.the_contrast_is_the_evidence: a DIRTY copy that survived is reported data_lost=[] by the partial handler and IS in data_lost when the SAME state is run through the full handler -- the two verdicts differ on identical state, which is precisely why one cannot stand in for the other

the_round_trip_blind_spot.the_hazard: the integrity check compares the SOURCE bytes against what copy_out RETURNS, so it validates THE ROUND TRIP. It does NOT validate THE RESIDENT COPY.
the_round_trip_blind_spot.why_that_is_not_pedantry: on a real bridge copy_out and a KERNEL are NOT THE SAME PATH -- one comes back over the transport, the other reads device memory directly. A provider whose compute path diverges from its read-back path PASSES verification and still computes on wrong bytes.
the_round_trip_blind_spot.demonstrated_not_asserted: compute_skew makes read_for_compute return different bytes from copy_out. The transfer verifies, the destination is CLEAN, its payload equals the source EXACTLY -- and what a kernel would read differs. A test pins all three facts together.
the_round_trip_blind_spot.there_is_no_cheap_fix_and_that_is_stated: catching it needs a check that reads through THE SAME PATH THE COMPUTATION USES, which means the DEVICE computing a digest of its own memory. That is a real design requirement for EGB and it is recorded rather than invented against a mock. The limit is now written where it lives -- in the verification block itself -- so `verified` cannot be read as a guarantee about what the GPU sees.
the_round_trip_blind_spot.relation_to_what_was_named: the previous receipt listed 'corruption AFTER the check' as unmodelled and this is a SHARPER version of it: not corruption after the check in TIME, but a check on the WRONG PATH entirely.

still_not_modelled: a provider that corrupts consistently in both directions such that the digest agrees with itself, and any adversary who can recompute a crc32 -- the checksum defends against ACCIDENT and is the wrong tool for a MALICIOUS peer

claim_boundary.mock_only: no external GPU exists. What is proven is the STATE MACHINE and the SCOPE OF THE CHECK, not any hardware property. Every transport number in this module remains a knob.
claim_boundary.the_probe_is_the_provider_itself: device_partially_lost asks the provider whether a copy survived. Against a real device that probe is itself a transport operation that can fail or hang, and the partial-loss handler does NOT wrap it in the deadline the transfer path uses -- an honest gap, named.
